what: PRB-1420, third part: every needs_review observation of occupation-full-publication-2026-10-27-v1 left after parts 1 and 2 whose kind names a military role or a trade (290 rows: 135 military, 155 trade), decided by reading the verses. Admitted claims are in ../person-occupations.json; this file says why, and why not. Requests and the loader never read it.
rules: The rules of parts 1 and 2 hold (prb-1420-part-1.json, prb-1420-part-2.json).

'Mighty men of valour' (גִּבּוֹרֵי חַיִל) in a genealogy's summary, with the count of the house's men, is the house's strength and standing, not a warrior's occupation of each man named; a headship the same verse states is held (1 Chr 5:24, 7:2, 7:7, 7:9).
A count by heads ('by the heads of their fathers ... 17,200 fit for war', 1 Chr 7:11) does not call each man named a head.
Warrior is the noun גִּבּוֹר said of a named man in war (2 Chr 28:7) or a list of fighting men headed so (1 Chr 12:24-29).
A king leading his own army holds King, not a military office besides.
A plural said by and of Jacob's sons (Gen 46:32-34, 47:3) is not said of each grandson the list of Gen 46 names.
'Son of' a guild (בֶּן־הָרַקָּחִים, בֶּן־הַצֹּרְפִי) is a member of it, as 'the sons of the priests' are priests (part 1).

A trade is named, or its verb said of the person as their work (Adam sent 'to till the ground'; David playing the harp before Saul 'as day by day'); one season's work (Isaac's sowing) or charity (Dorcas' garments) is not.

2 Chr 17:14-16: 'of Judah, the captains of thousands: Adnah the chief..., next to him Jehohanan the captain..., and next to him Amasiah son of Zichri... with him 200,000 mighty men'. The heading governs the list; Adnah and Jehohanan hold it on it.

Gen 3:23 'the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden to till the ground' (לַעֲבֹד אֶת־הָאֲדָמָה), the very words of the occupation; 2:15 'to work it and keep it'. The work he is sent to, said of him by name (3:17-23).
Neh 3:31 'Malchiah the goldsmith's son' (בֶּן־הַצֹּרְפִי), BSB 'one of the goldsmiths': 'son of' the guild, as Hananiah son of the perfumers (3:8); 3:32 'the goldsmiths' repair beside him.

1 Sam 16:16-23: Saul's servants seek 'a man who is a skilful player on the harp'; David is 'skilful in playing' (16:18) and 'took the harp and played with his hand' whenever the spirit came (16:23), 'as at other times' (18:10, 19:9). A standing service at the court, said of him by the narrator.
Neh 3:8 'Hananiah, son of the perfumers' (בֶּן־הָרַקָּחִים): 'son of' a guild is a member of it (BSB 'one of the perfumers'), as part 1 read 'the sons of the priests' as priests.
1 Chr 4:22-23: 'Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, Saraph... and Jashubi-lehem... These were the potters (הַיּוֹצְרִים)': the closing line says it of the men 4:22 names.

1 Chr 24:6 'Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the scribe, of the Levites, wrote them before the king': the title at the head of the chain (BSB 'the scribe Shemaiah') and the scribe's verb.

1 Chr 12:29 'Zadok, a young man mighty of valour, and of his father's house twenty-two captains', in the count of 'the heads armed for war' who came to David at Hebron (12:24). Read of the record the verse's word is annotated to.
2 Chr 28:7 'Zichri, a mighty man (גִּבּוֹר) of Ephraim, slew Maaseiah the king's son...', in Pekah's war against Judah: the noun of the occupation said of him in battle.
